title: Global Rain and Snow (IMERG)
source: NASA GPM IMERG precipitation, NASA Scientific Visualization Studio
description: A flat map of the whole Earth, showing a week of rain and snow measured by NASA's Global Precipitation Measurement satellites (IMERG), in half-hour steps. Rain is drawn in green, yellow and red (light to heavy); snow in light blue to purple. Rain bands sweep across the oceans from west to east, a belt of storms circles the tropics, and snow falls mostly near the poles.
listening_guide: Raindrops: each pluck is rain somewhere on Earth. More drops = more rain.
Left to right in your headphones = west to east on the map.
Higher drops = rain further north, lower drops = further south.
Low rumble and booms = heavy downpours (10 mm per hour or more).
The warm chord swells as rain spreads and fades as it shrinks; it changes and a chime rings at the start of every day.
